I've got a 2 part comment of sorts:

Part 1: Platitudes aren't really helpful and kind of infuriating. Perhaps quotes from TV shows even more so. Nonetheless, I don't know if this is a platitude, and it might be really stupid, but one thing that stuck in my mind when I was thinking about ending it was a line from that Game of Thrones show. One of the characters is talking about death and he says "death is so final, but life is full of possibilities."

I know it might be stupid, and I kinda laugh at taking philosophical/life advice from a TV show about tits and dragons, but it stuck with me.

Part 2: Given part 1, I decided "Fuck it. I'm going to go do something else. I could fail and end up dead in a ditch on the other side of the world, but hey, I'd be in the exact same spot as if I'd killed myself right now, but at least I'd have maybe a more interesting path getting there. Plus, who knows what could happen?"

My suggestion is to try this. If you're thinking about killing yourself and that's legitimately a possibility, take a moment to stop and realize just how free that makes you. Like seriously, existentially free. You can do anything, and I don't mean that in some stupid kid's birthday party kind of way.

Let me give you a hard example, since I think that's the biggest failing of just tossing out some bullshit platitude out there.

I was going to kill myself and I decided to sell all my shit, say goodbye to everyone I knew, and blindly move to a city I had never visited, in a country on a different continent, with a language I didn't speak.

Why the fuck not? If I failed, I was dead. I was dead anyways. That was over 2 years ago and it's been an amazing fucking 2 years. I've had so many experiences since then, met so many people, yadda yadda yadda.

One of the biggest things I learned from doing this is just how much of a bubble everyone is in.

I'm in a bubble right now. You're in a bubble right now. The thing is, you can't see the bubble until you leave the bubble.

When I was going to end it, the world around me was my bubble. My life at that time was my bubble. The customs of the people around me, their culture, their language, their priorities, behaviors, their outlooks on life, their expectations about work/life balance, EVERYTHING about what I thought existence was like was just apart of my bubble.

I moved to a new bubble and so much is different in big and small ways. The windows in my apartment open up in a different way that's really cool and useful. The wall outlets are different. There is a lot more variety of food. People have different views on work, on sex, on religion, on life. The things people instinctively answer "of course!" to are different from where I was.

It turned out pretty well so far. Even if it didn't, was still more interesting than death. Death is boring. If you're dead anyways, fuck it, do something cool. You're free.
